claims.statement: Configuration is stored as `config.toml` under the OS configuration directory plus `hteam`; a missing file loads as default, while saving creates the directory and rewrites the serialized configuration.

`config.toml`'s `AuthConfig` persists cookie credentials, optional access and refresh tokens, default board data, and cached board and user identifiers; `Config` also persists board metadata, variables, TUI preferences, and working hours.
A configuration is authenticated only when both `session_id` and `csrf_token` are present, and `HteamClient::with_auth` rejects unauthenticated configuration before creating a client.

Request headers include cookie and CSRF headers when both cookie values are configured, include a bearer authorization header independently when `access_token` exists, and use manually constructed cookies rather than a reqwest cookie store.

Login collects or accepts session and CSRF cookies, probes visible boards before persisting, resolves the post-auth board from explicit override, configured default, or single-board auto-selection, and saves the configuration only after a successful authentication test.
`Session::open` loads durable configuration and creates an authenticated client, providing the shared session construction path used by CLI, TUI, and MCP entrypoints.
Board resolution prioritizes an explicit override, then the configured default board, then a readable valid `~/.last_ticket` value.
Durable board switching updates the configured board, writes `~/.last_ticket`, upserts board display metadata and last-used time, and saves `config.toml`.
The TUI initializes board and preferences from the session configuration, normalizing hidden list names, and reports an error when no board can be resolved.
A TUI board switch clears board-specific UI state, updates the client's in-memory board before refresh, and attempts durable persistence without reverting the live switch if persistence fails.
Changing the client's board number only mutates its in-memory configuration and invalidates the cached board ID, preventing a board identifier learned for the old board from being reused.
The client resolves a missing board ID from cards, falls back from the Open list to non-empty lists, and caches the result only in its in-memory configuration.

The client obtains a missing user ID from active work or the last shift record and then writes the user-scoped identifier to both its in-memory configuration and `config.toml`, ignoring a save failure.
The interactive REPL loads and saves history at `~/.hteam_history`, while TUI status messages are appended best-effort to `tui.log` beneath the Hteam configuration directory.
Focused tests cover override and configured-default board resolution, board-name lookup behavior, project operation responses, and live board API decoding using a mock client.

The TUI persists hidden list names in `[tui].hidden_lists`, normalizes them to lowercase, and still fetches the underlying lists and cards so a hidden list can be shown again without another network fetch.

`[tui].known_projects` is a most-recently-used list of project ids with optional cached names; opening the projects popup auto-loads the first remembered project when no project is active, and selecting a remembered project loads that project id.

Board resolution uses a precedence chain of explicit override, configured board number, then `~/.last_ticket`, and login uses the same visible-board probe before persisting cookies and any selected board.

`operations::boards::switch_board` is the durable board-switch path: it updates the configured board number, writes `~/.last_ticket`, upserts board metadata with `last_used`, and saves the configuration.
`Config::is_authenticated()` only checks for `session_id` and `csrf_token`, while `Session::open()` loads config and constructs the authenticated client that CLI, TUI, and MCP entrypoints share.

The weekly objectives cache is fresh for 24 hours from `last_synced_at`, and the update-check cache is fresh for 6 hours from `last_checked_at`; both timestamps are stored in `config.toml` as RFC3339 strings.
The TUI resolves `theme.active` at startup and falls back to the default theme when the configured preset or custom theme file does not resolve.

`config.toml` is credential-bearing user-local state; it is not encrypted, and the code does not enforce restrictive permissions, so the workstation or deployment environment is the protection boundary.

`config.toml` is the main user-local persistence file for Hteam configuration; if it is missing, `Config::load()` falls back to defaults, and saving rewrites the whole pretty-serialized file after creating the directory tree as needed.

The persisted configuration includes auth cookies and board identity fields (`session_id`, `csrf_token`, optional bearer tokens, `board_number`, `board_id`, `user_id`), plus board metadata, TUI preferences, working hours, weekly-objective cache data, theme selection, and update-check metadata.
`Config::is_authenticated()` only requires `session_id` and `csrf_token`; the client uses that gate when building an authenticated session.

`Session::open()` is the shared startup path for authenticated entrypoints: it loads `Config` and constructs an authenticated `HteamClient`, so CLI, TUI, and MCP surfaces reuse the same session-loading logic instead of rebuilding it independently.

Request authentication uses the configured cookies and CSRF header when present, and only adds `Authorization: Bearer ...` when an access token exists; the bearer token supplements the cookie session rather than replacing it.

Login is update-safe: it clones the current config, injects the supplied cookies into the clone, probes authentication before persisting anything, and exits without saving new credentials if auth is unauthorized or the network probe fails.

Login resolves the active board only after authentication succeeds, preferring an explicit `--board`, then a still-visible configured board, then auto-selecting the only visible board; if no board is selected, it still saves cookies but leaves board switching to the user.
When login or board switching selects a board, Hteam persists the new `board_number`, writes `~/.last_ticket`, and upserts the board metadata entry with a current `last_used` timestamp.

Board-number resolution follows a single fallback chain: explicit override first, then the configured default, then the last board saved in `~/.last_ticket`; if none are available, the caller must treat a board as required.
`operations::boards::switch_board()` is the durable switching path and also clears the client's cached `board_id` in memory so later board-specific requests do not reuse the previous board identity.

The TUI reads `hidden_lists`, `known_projects`, `working_hours`, and `theme.active` from the session configuration at startup; hidden lists are normalized to lowercase, preference edits reload durable config before saving, and `known_projects` behaves as a most-recently-used list of project ids with optional cached names.

`working_hours` only affects display logic: when the configured range parses and the current time falls within it, the TUI can render the remaining-work-time footer; invalid or missing values simply suppress that footer.
`theme.active` is resolved at startup for rendering, and invalid built-in or custom theme names fall back to `default` with a warning rather than failing the TUI startup.
The weekly-objectives cache uses `last_synced_at` and a 24-hour TTL, while the update-check cache uses `last_checked_at` and a 6-hour TTL; these caches are separate from board-selection recency data.
`hteam interactive` loads the config at startup and shows the active board when one is configured, but it does not mutate persisted session state by itself.

The CLI parser exposes `--board` globally for board-scoped commands, while `tui`, `interactive`, and `mcp` derive their runtime behavior from the shared configuration layer rather than separate session systems.

Hteam persists user-local session and preference state in `config.toml` under the platform config directory plus companion files `~/.last_ticket`, `~/.hteam_history`, and `tui.log` in the config directory.

The persisted config schema includes auth cookies and cached board/user identity, board metadata with last-used timestamps, variables, TUI hidden-list and known-project MRU state, working-hours settings, weekly-objectives cache fields, theme selection, and update-check cache fields.
`Config::load()` tolerates a missing config file by returning defaults, while `Config::save()` rewrites the whole pretty-serialized file and creates parent directories when needed.

`Session::open()` is the shared startup path for authenticated entrypoints: it loads `Config` and builds an authenticated `HteamClient`, so CLI, TUI, and MCP surfaces inherit the same session-loading logic.

Authentication is considered present only when both `session_id` and `csrf_token` exist, and requests add `Authorization: Bearer ...` only when an access token is available; the bearer token supplements the cookie session instead of replacing it.

Login probes the API before persisting credentials: it clones the current config, injects the supplied cookies, calls `check_auth`, and exits without saving if the probe is unauthorized or returns a network error.

Post-auth board selection during login follows a strict precedence: explicit `--board` first, then a still-visible configured board, then automatic selection when exactly one board is visible; otherwise the caller is told to switch manually or that no Execution boards are available.

Successful login persistence writes the new cookies, optionally updates the configured board number, saves `~/.last_ticket`, and upserts the board name plus `last_used` timestamp into the `[boards.<id>]` map before saving `config.toml`.

Board-number resolution for runtime operations uses one precedence chain everywhere: explicit override, then the configured default board number, then `~/.last_ticket`; if none are present, callers must fail with a missing-board error instead of inventing a board.

`operations::boards::switch_board()` is the durable board-switch path: it updates the configured board number, saves `~/.last_ticket`, derives a display name from an explicit name, an existing board entry, or `Board <id>`, stamps `last_used`, and saves the config.
Board switching clears the client's cached `board_id` in memory so later board-specific API calls do not reuse the previous board identity.

The TUI loads `hidden_lists`, `known_projects`, `working_hours`, and `theme.active` from config at startup; hidden list names are normalized to lowercase, hidden lists still remain fetchable, and toggling list visibility reloads durable configuration before saving to avoid overwriting concurrent file changes.

`known_projects` is a persisted MRU of project ids with optional cached names; selecting or loading a project moves it to the front of the list, persists it to `[tui] known_projects`, and the projects popup auto-loads the first remembered project when no project is active yet.

`working_hours` only affects display logic: the TUI shows the remaining-work-time footer only when the configured range parses successfully and the current time falls inside that range; invalid or missing values suppress the footer.
`theme.active` is resolved once at TUI startup and falls back to `default` with a warning when it does not match a built-in theme or a parseable custom theme file.

Weekly-objectives caching is fresh only when `last_synced_at` parses as RFC3339 and is less than 24 hours old; if a cached title exists, the stored title and objectives can be reconstructed into a `WeeklyObjectivesSet`.
Update checking uses a separate persisted cache with a 6-hour freshness window; when fresh and a latest version is cached, the startup update flow reuses that version instead of calling GitHub again.

The CLI exposes `--board` globally for board-scoped commands, while `interactive`, `tui`, and `mcp` all derive their runtime behavior from the shared configuration and session-loading path rather than maintaining separate config systems.
`hteam interactive` loads config at startup and prints the active board when one is configured, but it does not mutate persisted session state by itself.
`config.toml` is not encrypted and the code does not enforce restrictive permissions, so the workstation or deployment environment is the protection boundary for secrets stored there.
